params.body:
Five cron jobs never started, element tagging among them. Foresight has compared two empty periods since July.

cron runs a line as `/bin/sh -c '<command>'`, and `pgrep -f` matches every process's full command line, that shell included. The guard `pgrep -f "[t]ag-elements.mjs"` hides only the pgrep: its parent shell's command line also contains `packages/pipeline/tag-elements.mjs`, so the guard always found "a copy already running" and skipped. Reproduced on the box with a harmless line: the bracket guard sees itself, an anchored guard does not.

On production: 2,599 signals tagged in May, 3,420 in June, 4 in July, none since. `logs/tag-elements.log` and `logs/link-trends.log` do not exist.

- `ops/crontab`: the five guards (discover, collect, classify, link-trends, tag-elements) are anchored on the node process, `^/usr/bin/node packages/pipeline/<script>.mjs`, as the china worker line already was. The comment above them says why.
- `test/cron-guards.test.mjs`: every guarded line must not match its own `sh -c` command line and must match the node process it guards. Fails 5 on the old file.
- `countTaggedElements` reports `newestTagged`, and `getElementShifts` reports how many tagged signals each period holds, so Foresight can say that the tagger stopped instead of "nothing has moved" (dashboard PR alongside).
- `test/foresight-coverage.test.mjs`. 982 tests pass.

After merge the crontab on the box needs `bin/crontab-install --apply`; a deploy does not install it. Once tagging runs (150 signals an hour), the 46,712 waiting signals from the last 120 days take about 13 days; the last 30 days fill much sooner because the tagger picks at random. link-trends will also run for the first time at 08:30 the next morning (at most ten new trends, agreed links only).
params.title: Cron guards: five jobs never started, element tagging among them
